words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa, ppp. ava-√sañj

hindi: एरण्ड के सीसक पर लगाया गया, एरण्ड की आग पर भूना गया और एरण्ड के तेल से युक्त मोर का मांस तुरन्त मार डालता है।
english: Peacock meat fixed on a castor (eraṇḍa) sīsaka, scorched on a castor fire and combined with castor oil, kills at once.

text_flags.why: the same word is printed eraṇḍa (retroflex ḍa) twice in this line; ṇd is a typing slip

notes: sīsaka ordinarily means lead; with avasakta 'fixed on, hung on' and the castor fire in the same line it seems here to mean a spit or skewer, but the meaning is uncertain and the word is kept in both translations. eraṇḍa = Ricinus communis (standard). Prose line.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa, ppp. ava-√sañj
n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member), ppp. pari-√dhvaṃs

hindi: हारिद्रक का मांस, हारिद्र के सीसक पर लगाया गया और हारिद्र की आग पर भूना गया, तुरन्त मार डालता है; वही राख और धूल से ढका हुआ, शहद के साथ, तत्काल मृत्यु के लिए होता है।
english: Hāridraka meat fixed on a hāridra sīsaka and scorched on a hāridra fire kills at once; that same (meat), covered with ash and dust and taken with honey, is for immediate death.
notes: hāridraka (the animal whose meat is meant) and hāridra (the wood of the spit and fire) are left unidentified; hāridra is formally 'of haridrā'. sīsaka as in P29: meaning uncertain (lead, or here a spit). Prose line.

words.gloss: prepared in the frying of fish

hindi: मत्स्य-निस्तालन में सिद्ध की गई पिप्पलियाँ, तथा काकमाची और मधु (साथ में) मृत्यु के लिए होते हैं।
english: Long peppers (pippalī) prepared in the frying of fish (matsyanistālana), and likewise kākamācī and honey (together), lead to death.
notes: nistālana is taken as 'frying' from the context of cooking; the medium (the oil or the pan used for the fish) is not stated, and the word's exact sense is uncertain. Whether kākamācī and honey are meant together (as a combination) or each separately is not explicit; the combination reading fits the list of incompatible pairs. pippalī = Piper longum (standard); kākamācī = Solanum nigrum (standard). Prose line.

hindi: और उष्ण मधु, और उष्णता से पीड़ित व्यक्ति के लिए मधु, मृत्यु के लिए होता है।
english: Hot honey, and honey for one afflicted by heat, lead to death.
notes: The opening ca links this line to the preceding list. Prose line.

words.gloss: roasted on a spit over charcoal

hindi: समान मात्रा में मधु और घी; मधु और आन्तरिक्ष जल समान मात्रा में; मधु और पुष्कर-बीज; मधु पीकर उष्ण जल; भल्लातक और उष्ण जल; तक्र में सिद्ध कम्पिल्लक; बासी काकमाची; और अङ्गारों पर सलाख में भुना भास — ये विरुद्ध हैं।
english: Honey and ghee in equal measure; honey and rain-water in equal measure; honey and lotus seed (puṣkarabīja); hot water after drinking honey; bhallātaka with hot water; kampillaka prepared in buttermilk; stale kākamācī; and bhāsa roasted on a spit over charcoal: these are incompatible.
notes: vāri āntarikṣam = rain-water (water from the sky). bhāsa is an animal whose meat is meant (roasted on a spit); left unidentified. bhallātakoṣṇodakam is split as one samāhāra unit 'bhallātaka with hot water' by analogy with the pairs before it. Identifications: puṣkara = lotus, Nelumbo nucifera (probable); bhallātaka = Semecarpus anacardium (standard); kampillaka = Mallotus philippensis (probable); kākamācī = Solanum nigrum (standard). Prose line.

hindi: इस प्रकार यह प्रश्न के अनुसार निर्दिष्ट हो गया है।
english: Thus this has been set out according to the question.

text_flags.why: the participle must agree with etad (n. nom. sg.), so -aṃ not -āṃ; and ṣt is not a possible cluster (ṣṭ)

notes: Prose line.

hindi: और यहाँ (श्लोक) हैं: जो कोई भी आहार दोष को प्रवाहित करके उसे शरीर से बाहर नहीं निकालता, वह सब अहित के लिए होता है।
english: And here there are: Whatever kind of food sets a doṣa flowing but does not remove it from the body, all that turns out to be harmful.
notes: āsrāvya (causative of ā-√sru) is taken literally as 'having set flowing', i.e. having stirred the doṣa from its place.

words.gloss: by place, time, digestive fire, measure, suitability, Vāta and the rest
words.gram: m. inst. pl., dvandva ending in ādi (bahuvrīhi)

hindi: और जो भी देश, काल, अग्नि, मात्रा, सात्म्य, वात आदि से, संस्कार से और वीर्य से, तथा कोष्ठ, अवस्था और क्रम से भी (विरुद्ध हो),
english: And that also which (is incompatible) by place, time, digestive fire, measure, suitability (sātmya), Vāta (anila) and the rest, by processing and by potency (vīrya), and also by bowel (koṣṭha), state and sequence,
notes: SENTENCE: 86 and 87 form one sentence; the main clause 'viruddhaṃ tac ca na hitam' is in 87. anila-ādi = Vāta and the other doṣas.

words.gloss: by restriction and manner of use

hindi: परिहार और उपचार से, पाक से और संयोग से भी (विरुद्ध हो), वह विरुद्ध है और हितकर नहीं है; तथा जो हृदय, सम्पत् और विधि से (विरुद्ध हो)।
english: by restriction (parihāra) and manner of use (upacāra), by cooking and also by combination — that is incompatible and not wholesome, and (so is) what (is incompatible) by heart (hṛd), excellence (sampad) and rule (vidhi).
notes: SENTENCE: continues 86. COUNT: the list in 86-87 names eighteen kinds (place, time, agni, measure, sātmya, the doṣas, processing, potency, bowel, state, sequence, restriction, upacāra, cooking, combination, heart, excellence, rule). The definitions that follow (88-101) take them in this order, but upacāra has no separately named definition in this chunk; the second half of 98 (cold after ghee) may be meant for it. 'hṛtsaṃpadvidhibhiḥ' is grammatically gender-mixed; m. given for the plural compound.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva ending in ādi
n. nom. sg., dvandva ending in ādi

hindi: पहले, देश से विरुद्ध: धन्व देश में रूक्ष, तीक्ष्ण आदि, और आनूप देश में स्निग्ध, शीत आदि जो भेषज सेवन किया जाता है।
english: First, incompatible by place: the medicine, dry, sharp and the like, that is used in a dry region (dhanvan), or unctuous, cold and the like in a marshy region (ānūpa).

text_flags.why: tīkṣaṇa is not a word (tīkṣṇa 'sharp'); with tīkṣaṇa the pāda has 9 syllables, with tīkṣṇa the required 8

words.gloss: use of cold, dry and the like
use of pungent, hot and the like

hindi: काल से भी विरुद्ध वह है जो शीत काल में शीत, रूक्ष आदि का सेवन है, तथा उष्ण (काल) में कटु, उष्ण आदि का सेवन।
english: Incompatible by time also is the use of cold, dry and similar things in the cold season, and likewise the use of pungent, hot and similar things in the hot (season).

hindi: इसी प्रकार चार प्रकार के अनल से विरुद्ध अन्न-पान (होता है)। समान मात्रा में मधु और घी — वह मात्रा से विरुद्ध होता है।
english: Likewise, (there is) food and drink incompatible with the fourfold digestive fire (anala). Honey and ghee in equal measure: that is incompatible by measure.
notes: The locative anale is taken as 'with regard to the digestive fire'; the four kinds of fire are not named in this chunk.

words.gloss: for one to whom pungent, hot and the like are suitable
use of sweet, cold and the like

hindi: कटु, उष्ण आदि जिसके लिए सात्म्य हों, उसके द्वारा मधुर, शीत आदि का जो सेवन है, वह सात्म्य-विरुद्ध है; और वात आदि से विरुद्ध —
english: For one to whom pungent, hot and similar things are suitable (sātmya), the use of sweet, cold and similar things: that is incompatible with suitability. And incompatible with Vāta (anila) and the rest
notes: SENTENCE: the last clause (incompatible with Vāta and the rest) is completed by 92a.

words.gloss: use of food and herbs incompatible through habitual use of the same qualities

hindi: (वह है) जो समान गुणों के अभ्यास से विरुद्ध अन्न और औषधि का प्रयोग है। संस्कार से विरुद्ध वह है, जो भोज्य विष के समान हो जाए —
english: is the use of food and herbs that is incompatible through habitual use of the same qualities (as theirs). Incompatible by processing is that food which would become like poison,
notes: SENTENCE: 92a completes 91b; 92b runs on into 93a. The long compound is ambiguous: it may also be read as 'the use of food and medicine of the same qualities (as Vāta etc.), and incompatible (made so) by habitual use'. auṣadhi (herb) is kept as printed beside the more usual auṣadha (medicine); the sense is the same here.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa, ppp. ā-√sañj

hindi: ठीक जैसे एरण्ड के सीसक पर लगाया गया मोर का मांस। वीर्य से विरुद्ध उसे जानना चाहिए — जो वीर्य में शीतल स्वभाव वाला (द्रव्य)
english: just as peacock meat fixed on a castor sīsaka. Incompatible by potency (vīrya) is to be known (this): what is cold in nature as to potency
notes: SENTENCE: 93a completes 92b; 93b runs on into 94a. śikhin 'the crested one' = peacock, as mayūra in P29 of this chunk (the same preparation). sīsaka: see P29.

words.gloss: for one with a hard bowel

hindi: उसे उष्णवीर्य द्रव्य के साथ मिलाकर सेवन किया जाता है। और क्रूर कोष्ठ वाले के लिए अत्यल्प, मन्दवीर्य और अभेदक (द्रव्य),
english: is taken combined with a substance of hot potency. And for one with a hard bowel (krūrakoṣṭha), (what is) very little, of mild potency and non-purgative,
notes: SENTENCE: 94a completes 93b; 94b runs on into 95a.

words.gloss: for one with a soft bowel

words.gram: n. nom. sg., gerundive (kṛtya) √bhid, used as adj.

hindi: और मृदु कोष्ठ वाले के लिए गुरु, भेदक तथा अधिक — यह कोष्ठ-विरुद्ध है; और अवस्था से विरुद्ध होगा —
english: and for one with a soft bowel (mṛdukoṣṭha), (what is) heavy, purgative and likewise much: this is incompatible with the bowel (koṣṭha). And incompatible by state (avasthā) would be
notes: SENTENCE: the last clause is completed by 96.

words.gloss: for one given to fatigue, sexual intercourse and exercise
words.gram: m. gen. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: श्रम, व्यवाय और व्यायाम में लगे हुए व्यक्ति के लिए वात को कुपित करने वाला (भोजन), और निद्रा से अलसाए आलसी व्यक्ति के लिए कफ को कुपित करने वाला भोजन।
english: food aggravating Vāta (anila) for one given to fatigue, sexual intercourse (vyavāya) and exercise, and food aggravating Kapha (śleṣman) for one who is languid with sleep and lazy.
notes: SENTENCE: completes 95b. bhojanam is understood with anilakopanam too. nidrālasasyālasasya may also be divided nidrā-ālasya (sleep and lethargy) + alasasya, or read as two genitives of one person; the sense is the same.

words.gloss: (one) under the sway of excessive hunger

hindi: और जो मल-मूत्र का त्याग किए बिना खाता है, और जो भूख न होने पर खाता है, वह क्रम-विरुद्ध होता है; और जो अत्यधिक भूख के वश में होकर (खाता है)।
english: And when one eats without voiding faeces and urine, and one who eats when not hungry: that would be incompatible by sequence (krama); and (so is) what (is eaten by one) under the sway of excessive hunger.
notes: The construction is loose: yat (n.) is paired with the masculine yaḥ and ...anugaḥ (the eater); 'one who eats' is understood in each clause. viṭ-mūtra is a samāhāra dvandva (neuter singular), as printed in one compound.

hindi: परिहार से विरुद्ध वह है, जब कोई सूअर आदि का सेवन करके उष्ण का सेवन करे; और घी आदि पीकर शीतल का सेवन करता है।
english: And incompatible by restriction (parihāra) is when, having eaten boar and the like, one takes something hot, and (when), having drunk ghee and the like, one takes something cold.
notes: The second clause (cold after ghee) is joined to parihāra by ca as printed; it may be the example meant for upacāra, which is listed in 87 but not separately named in this chunk.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa, ppp. caus. √sādh

words.gloss: with rice left raw, overcooked or burnt
words.gram: n. nom. sg., bahuvrīhi / dvandva of adjectives

hindi: पाक से भी विरुद्ध वह है जो दूषित और बुरे ईंधन-काष्ठ से पकाया गया हो, और जो कच्चे चावल वाला, अत्यधिक पका हुआ या जला हुआ हो; संयोग से विरुद्ध वह है, जैसे दूध के साथ अम्ल।
english: Incompatible by cooking also is what is prepared with spoiled, bad fuel-wood, and what is (cooked) with the rice left raw, overcooked or burnt; incompatible by combination is, for example, something sour with milk.

text_flags.why: possible: the feminine ending -ā has nothing to agree with; yat and viruddham in the same verse are neuter

notes: The compound in 99b may be read as 'raw-rice, overcooked and burnt' (three faults) or with apakvataṇḍula as one item; the sense is the same.

hindi: और जो मन को रुचिकर न हो, वह हृदय-विरुद्ध कहा जाता है। सम्पत्-विरुद्ध उसे जानना चाहिए जिसका रस उत्पन्न न हुआ हो,
english: And what is not pleasing to the mind is called incompatible with the heart (hṛd). One should know as incompatible with excellence (sampad) that whose taste has not developed,
notes: SENTENCE: the definition of sampad-viruddha continues in 101a.

words.gloss: whose taste has passed its time

words.gram: n. nom. sg., ppp. caus. upa-√yuj

hindi: या जिसका रस बीत चुका हो, या जिसका रस बिगड़ ही गया हो। और विधि-विरुद्ध उसे जानना चाहिए जो एकान्त में नहीं खाया जाता। इस प्रकार का अन्न प्रयोग किए जाने पर विरुद्ध होता है।
english: or whose taste has passed its time, or whose taste is indeed spoiled. And to be known as incompatible with the rule (vidhi) is what is not eaten in privacy. Food of such kinds, when used, would be incompatible.
notes: SENTENCE: 101a completes 100b. evaṃvidham is taken as one word 'of such kind'.

words.gloss: of impotence, blindness, vīsarpa and dakodara
of fainting, intoxication, ādhmāna and galagraha

hindi: विरुद्ध अन्न को नपुंसकता, अन्धता, वीसर्प, दकोदर, विस्फोटक, उन्माद, भगन्दर, मूर्च्छा, मद, आध्मान, गलग्रह, पाण्डु रोग और आमविष का,
english: (Incompatible food, they declare, is the cause) of impotence (ṣāṇḍhya), blindness, vīsarpa, dakodara, visphoṭaka, insanity (unmāda), bhagandara, fainting (mūrcchā), intoxication (mada), ādhmāna, galagraha, the disease pāṇḍu, and āmaviṣa,
notes: SENTENCE: 102 and 103 form one sentence; the verb pravadanti is in 103b. Upajāti (indravajrā) metre; vīsarpa with long ī is required by the metre. dakodara is taken as daka-udara (udara with water); āmaviṣa as 'āma-poison'; names kept Sanskrit, no modern identifications. The gender given for the mixed dvandvas follows the last member.

words.gloss: of kilāsa, kuṣṭha and grahaṇī disease
of swelling, amlapitta, fever and pīnasa

hindi: किलास, कुष्ठ और ग्रहणी रोग का, शोथ, अम्लपित्त, ज्वर और पीनस का, सन्तान-दोष का और उसी प्रकार मृत्यु का कारण बताते हैं।
english: of kilāsa, kuṣṭha and grahaṇī disease, of swelling (śotha), amlapitta, fever (jvara) and pīnasa, of defects in offspring, and likewise of death.
notes: SENTENCE: completes 102. grahaṇī-gada may also be read with gada governing all three ('the diseases kilāsa, kuṣṭha and grahaṇī'). Disease names kept Sanskrit.

hindi: इन और अन्य विरोध-जनित रोगों के ये भाव प्रतिकार हैं — जैसे वमन और विरेचन, और उनके विरोधी द्रव्यों का शमन के लिए प्रयोग, तथा वैसे द्रव्यों से पहले ही शरीर का संस्कार।
english: Of these and of other diseases caused by incompatibility, the following are the remedies: namely, emesis and purgation, the use of substances opposed to those (incompatibles) for pacifying them, and the prior conditioning of the body with substances of that kind.
notes: This unit is prose typed as two verse lines (no metre). tadvirodhinām is taken as 'opposed to those (incompatible things)'; it may also mean 'opposed to those (diseases)'.

hindi: और यहाँ दो (श्लोक) हैं: विरुद्ध भोजन से उत्पन्न रोगों को विवेचन, वमन और शमन, अथवा पहले से हितकर का सेवन नष्ट करता है।
english: And here there are two: Purgation (vivecana), emesis and pacifying (śamana), or the prior use of what is wholesome, counters diseases born of incompatible eating.
notes: The singular verb pratihanti goes with each of the listed measures. vivecana (literally 'separating out') is taken as purgation, since emesis is named separately.

words.gloss: for one with keen digestive fire
for the unctuous, exercised and strong

hindi: सात्म्य होने से, अथवा अल्प मात्रा में होने से भी, और प्रदीप्त अग्नि वाले तथा युवा के लिए, तथा स्निग्ध, व्यायाम करने वाले और बलवान लोगों के लिए विरुद्ध निष्फल हो जाता है।
english: Through suitability (sātmya), or also through small quantity, and for one with keen digestive fire and the young, and for those who are unctuous, used to exercise and strong, the incompatible becomes ineffective.
notes: snigdha-vyāyāma-balinām may also be read 'for those strong through unction and exercise'. vitatha literally 'untrue, futile'.

hindi: यहाँ श्लोक हैं: रस-निर्णय के विषय में महर्षियों का जो-जो मत था; गुण और कर्म के अनुसार द्रव्य; रस पर आश्रित द्रव्य-संख्या;
english: Here, the verses: whatever opinion the great sages each held on the determination of taste; substances by their qualities and actions; the number of substances based on taste;

text_flags.why: krama + bhyām would give kramābhyām, so the printed form is not grammatical; guṇakarman (quality and action) appears in 110 of this chunk (guṇakarmaṇi); the metre is unchanged

notes: SENTENCE: the summary verses 107-113 form one sentence, a list of topics ending in 113 'all that the sage told in the Ātreyabhadrakāpyīya'.

words.gloss: the characteristic of rasa and anurasa
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: रसों की संख्या का कारण; रस और अनुरस का लक्षण; और पर आदि गुणों के अलग-अलग लक्षण;
english: the reason for the number of tastes; the characteristic of rasa and anurasa (secondary taste); and the characteristics of the qualities beginning with para, each separately;

hindi: और जिस कारण से पञ्चात्मक रस छह हैं; और जिस गुण की अधिकता से रस ऊर्ध्वगामी और अनुलोमगामी होते हैं;
english: the reason by which the tastes, being composed of the five (pañcātmaka), are six; and from the excess of which quality the tastes tend upward or downward;

hindi: छह रसों के षट्त्व के विषय में उप-विभागों सहित विभाग; और द्रव्यों के गुण-कर्म के विषय में उद्देश और अपवाद;
english: the divisions, with their subdivisions, regarding the sixfoldness of the six tastes; and the general statement and the exception about the quality and action of substances;
notes: savibhaktāḥ 'with their subdivisions' is a literal rendering; what the divisions are is not stated in this chunk.

words.gloss: determination of the number of potencies

hindi: गुरुता आदि में रसों का श्रेष्ठ, अवर और मध्य होना; पाक और प्रभाव का लक्षण; वीर्य-संख्या का निश्चय;
english: the highest, lowest and middle rank of the tastes in heaviness and the rest; the sign of vipāka (pāka, post-digestive taste) and prabhāva (specific action); the determination of the number of vīryas (potencies);

text_flags.why: gaurva is not a word (gaurava 'heaviness'); with gaurva the pāda has 7 syllables, with gaurava the required 8

notes: rasānām is printed with m before a consonant (for ṃ); this is only spelling and is kept.

words.gram: m. gen. pl., pres. pass. part. caus. ā-√svad

hindi: चखे जाते हुए छह रसों का जो स्वलक्षण है; जो-जो जिससे विरुद्ध होता है, जिसके द्वारा, और जो जिस कार्य को करने वाला है;
english: the own characteristic (svalakṣaṇa) of the six tastes as they are tasted; whatever is incompatible with whatever, through what, and what each one produces;
notes: The relative clauses in 112b are compressed; yasmāt is taken as 'with what' (the thing it conflicts with) and yena as 'through what (cause)'.

hindi: और विरोध से उत्पन्न रोगों की जो औषध है — वह सब मुनि ने आत्रेयभद्रकाप्यीय में कहा।
english: and the medicine for diseases caused by incompatibility: all that the sage told in the Ātreyabhadrakāpyīya.

text_flags.why: vyāhīnām is not a word; the same phrase vairodhikanimittānāṃ vyādhīnām is printed in 104 of this chunk

notes: avadan is avadat before muniḥ (t becomes n before a nasal); no error. Chapter name in -īya kept unsplit.

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित, चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में आत्रेयभद्रकाप्यीय नामक छब्बीसवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, in the Śloka section (Ślokasthāna), the twenty-sixth chapter named Ātreyabhadrakāpyīya.
notes: Chapter colophon (prose).
